newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says air embargo caused 1,918 deaths.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says air embargo caused 1,918 deaths.

text.p: The air embargo on Iraq has caused the death of 1,918 people since it was imposed in 1990 for Baghdad's invasion of Kuwait, Health Minister Umeed Mubarak was quoted as saying on Tuesday.
He said patients who needed treatment abroad had to travel by land to Jordan and several had died on the way.
Treatment for heart diseases and cancer was mostly concentrated in Baghdad and patients throughout the country had to travel long distances to reach the capital.

"The process of carrying these patients from far away provinces to Baghdad...requires the use of land roads which in turn takes long time and effort often resulting in their death," Mubarak said in a statement to the official Iraqi News Agency.
"The state of suffering is beyond description in which Iraq loses daily many patients among them children, women and the elderly, he said.
He said Iraq lacked ambulances to transfer its patients from one place to another and treatment outside Iraq was almost now impossible.

The U.N. trade sanctions imposed on Iraq for invading Kuwait in 1990 bar international flights by Baghdad. Local flights are also not possible due to the existence of two Western-protected no-fly zones in the country-- one in the south and another in the north.
Mubarak called on U.N. organisations and humanitarian agencies in the world to work together to "save Iraqi patients and ease their suffering."
